items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: When did you join the McShann band, and when did you leave New York?
I joined McShann’s band around ’48, and we worked our way back to California. I met the band in Birmingham, Alabama. Took the bus down there [laughs].

items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: Art played with the group I had over

ctx.x: There's not a chance in the world. With all due respect to Art. Art played with the group I had over

on the coast. He played with me and his brother played with me, too, on bass. You know? But their conception -- see, here's what I mean. Speaking of conceptions, he would be better, you know what I mean, with a group that's thinking in terms of Diz and even including the bass player, drummers that think in those terms, better than put him in a group that is swinging. See? You put him in a group that's swinging, he's lost. But you put him in a technical group, he's at home.
